hypotheses.title: Higher anion coordination predicts a stronger LiF-rich interphase signature under matched conditions
hypotheses.statement: Within matched high-voltage fast-charging lithium-metal electrolyte variants, increasing anion coordination relative to a lower-anion-coordination control will increase the LiF-rich interphase signature.

independent_variable.name: anion coordination strength
independent_variable.manipulation_or_contrast: Higher versus lower anion coordination in otherwise matched electrolyte variants.

dependent_variable.name: LiF-rich interphase signature
dependent_variable.measurement_or_observation: A predefined LiF-sensitive interphase metric measured consistently across the compared variants.

expected_relation.detail: The higher-anion-coordination condition is expected to show a stronger predefined LiF-rich interphase signature than the lower-coordination condition.

hypotheses.scientific_significance: If supported, the hypothesis would show whether anion coordination is a transferable interphase-design variable rather than only a descriptor of one reported formulation.
hypotheses.mechanism_reasoning: The supplied evidence links anion-rich solvation to LiF-rich interphase formation and high Coulombic efficiency in the reported system. This motivates testing anion coordination as a variable, but does not establish the proposed cross-formulation relation.
hypotheses.falsifiable_prediction: When the intended anion-coordination contrast is present within the stated boundary, the higher-anion-coordination condition will show a reproducibly higher predefined LiF-rich interphase metric than the lower-coordination condition.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: The hypothesis is falsified within the stated boundary if the intended anion-coordination contrast is present but the higher-anion-coordination condition does not show a reproducibly higher predefined LiF-rich interphase metric.
hypotheses.known_evidence_boundary: Existing evidence supports the anion-rich-solvation to LiF-rich-interphase relationship in the reported LiFSI/FDEE system, but does not establish that increasing anion coordination across matched alternative formulations causes a stronger LiF-rich interphase signature.
uncertainties: Anion coordination may covary with solvent chemistry or concentration.
The interphase signal may not uniquely represent the mechanism responsible for Coulombic-efficiency retention.
